extracted.intended_audience: SEC registrants, corporate accountants, auditors and financial reporting professionals working on business combination / acquisition disclosure
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on performing the three SEC significance tests (investment, income, asset) when an entity acquires a business, including how to compute numerators/denominators, thresholds, treatment of intercompany items, related businesses and contingent consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elimination of intercompany transactions for significance tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Intercompany transactions between the registrant and the acquired business are eliminated as if the acquired business had always been consolidated when performing the significance tests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminations may affect the numerator, the denominator, or both depending on the nature of the intercompany transaction. Elimination is done solely for performing the significance tests — historical financial statements of the acquired business filed with the SEC are not adjusted to remove transactions with the registrant. Examples: exclude preferred stock dividends received by the acquired company; exclude investments in registrant held by the acquired entity when performing the asset test; exclude intercompany revenue and intercompany profit from income/revenue components. (See S‑X Rule 1‑02(w), FRM citations and multiple worked examples.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test — pretax income component
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate the pretax income component by adjusting the acquired business’s pretax income from continuing operations to exclude intercompany profit, then dividing the adjusted amount by the registrant’s pretax income from continuing operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform: (Acquired business’ unadjusted pretax income − intercompany profit = adjusted pretax income) ÷ Registrant’s pretax income. When acquiring related businesses, combine the income/loss of related businesses first (take absolute value of combined income or loss). Worked examples show excluding intercompany profit even when the acquired business was previously consolidated (no adjustment to registrant's own pretax income if consolidation eliminations already exist). The income test uses the lower of the pretax income and revenue component results for the income-test outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test — revenue component
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate the revenue component by excluding intercompany revenue from the acquired business’s total revenues and dividing the adjusted revenues by the registrant’s revenues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform: (Acquired business’ unadjusted revenues − intercompany revenue = adjusted revenues) ÷ Registrant’s revenues. For related businesses, use combined revenue of all related businesses; the revenue component only applies if combined revenue is material for each of the last two years. If the revenue component applies, SEC financial statement requirements depend on whether both revenue and pretax income components exceed quantitative thresholds (see guidance on 20% test).

rubrics_metrics.name: Asset test
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the asset test by dividing the acquired business’s assets to be acquired (after excluding intercompany assets) by the registrant’s adjusted total assets (after eliminations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform: Company A’s assets to be acquired ÷ Registrant’s adjusted total assets (after eliminations). Intercompany carrying amounts such as inventory purchased from the acquired business or receivables from the registrant are excluded from the acquired business’s assets for the test. Examples show excluding purchased inventory still held by registrant and excluding intercompany receivables when the acquired business was previously consolidated (no registrant adjustment needed if consolidated eliminations already removed them). The overall acquisition significance is determined by the highest level of significance across the three tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test — threshold & overall decision rule (handbook guidance)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance under the investment test (per section 3.4.10) is met when the registrant’s and its subsidiaries’ investments in and advances to the acquired business exceed 20% of the registrant’s AWMV (Aggregate Worldwide Market Value); if AWMV is not available use consolidated total assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform investment test as: (Investments in and advances to acquired business) ÷ (Registrant’s AWMV if available; otherwise consolidated total assets). Decision tree: if result > 20% → acquisition is significant (for investment test); if not, complete income and asset tests to determine overall significance. Note: the guidance includes worked examples (working capital loan included in consideration, long‑term notes included as advances) demonstrating numerator composition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment test — S‑X Rule 1‑02 alternate threshold language
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation S‑X excerpt (S‑X Rule 1‑02(w)) provides alternate formulations for the investment test and related thresholds, including references to 10% in specific contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The S‑X excerpt on 'Significant subsidiary' states, for acquisitions (other than those in paragraph (B)) and dispositions the test is met when investments/advances exceed 10% of AWMV or, if no AWMV, total assets as of the end of the most recently completed fiscal year. For combinations between entities under common control paragraph (B) provides different 10% tests based on net book value or shares exchanged. The handbook text elsewhere (3.4.10) uses a 20% threshold for the investment test — practitioners should follow the applicable regulatory/statutory source and the Handbook commentary together to determine the correct threshold for the specific SEC requirement being applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determining the numerator for the investment test (consideration transferred)
rubrics_metrics.description: The numerator is the registrant’s and its subsidiaries’ investments in and advances to the acquired business, generally equal to the GAAP purchase price (consideration transferred), adjusted in specified ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjustments: exclude the carrying amount of assets transferred by the acquirer to the acquired business that will remain with the combined entity; include fair value of contingent consideration if required to be recognized at fair value by applicable GAAP; when contingent consideration is not measured at fair value, include all contingent amounts except payments whose likelihood is remote. Include advances made in contemplation of the acquisition (e.g., working capital loans not repaid at consummation) and long‑term notes made to sellers where Company A is designated as lender — such amounts form part of consideration transferred. See examples showing numeric computation (e.g., working capital loan included resulting in significance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingent consideration treatment in the numerator
rubrics_metrics.description: Treatment of contingent consideration depends on applicable GAAP and accounting transaction type: include fair‑value‑measured contingent consideration; if not measured at fair value include contingent consideration unless likelihood of payment is remote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For business combinations under Topic 805, fair value of contingent consideration recognized at acquisition date is included. For equity method investments or asset acquisitions, different GAAP rules (e.g., Subtopic 323‑10, 805‑50, Topic 815) affect whether contingent consideration is included in the numerator; contingent consideration measured at fair value under other GAAP (e.g., derivatives under Topic 815) is included. The SEC staff has stated that significance need not be remeasured for subsequent fair value estimate changes if registrant made a good‑faith estimate at acquisition. Worked examples show inclusion or exclusion depending on whether payment is 'remote' or 'more than remote.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Denominator — Aggregate Worldwide Market Value (AWMV) calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: When using AWMV as the denominator, determine the aggregate worldwide market value of the registrant’s voting and non‑voting common equity using the average of such AWMV calculated daily for the last five trading days of the registrant’s most recently completed month ending prior to the earlier of the registrant’s announcement date or agreement date of the acquisition or disposition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the registrant has no AWMV, use consolidated total assets (as of end of most recently completed fiscal year) as the denominator. This averaging rule governs the timing and computation of the market‑value denominator for the investment test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Related businesses — when to aggregate for significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Businesses are considered related and tested on an as‑if combined basis when there is common control or common management, or when acquisitions are conditioned on a single common event or on the acquisition of another business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If acquired businesses are related, determine significance using the as‑if combined financial statements of all related businesses. When multiple related businesses are acquired at different times during the year, perform a cumulative significance test at the consummation date of each new acquisition in the series using the registrant’s last audited annual financial statements required to be filed. When new audited financial statements for a subsequent fiscal year are filed, start a new accumulation group using those newly filed statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate asset and investment tests for groups of related businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: To perform aggregate asset or investment tests for related business acquisitions, perform the applicable test for each individual business and add the individual results to arrive at a combined (aggregate) result.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asset test: separately compute each acquired business’s asset test result then add them. Investment test: separately compute each acquired business’s investment test result then add them. (FRM references cited.) Use the combined results to evaluate significance for the group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Income test for related businesses (aggregate income test rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: For related businesses, treat them as a single business combination for the income test by combining income (or loss) and revenue of all related businesses and using the combined amounts to perform the pretax income and revenue components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine income/loss from continuing operations before income taxes for all related businesses to arrive at combined income or loss, then take absolute value when computing the pretax income component. Combine revenues for the revenue component. If the combined revenue is material for each of the last two years, the quantitative result of the revenue component applies. If revenue component applies, financial statement requirements (for SEC filing) depend on whether both revenue and pretax income components exceed 20% (see cross‑reference to further discussion). This combined approach applies regardless of whether related businesses are under common control or common management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumulative significance when acquisitions follow a combination under common control
rubrics_metrics.description: When a registrant acquires a business after previously combining entities under common control (accounted for at historical cost using as‑if pooling‑of‑interests), determine significance using the retrospectively restated as‑if pooled financial statements for the most recently completed fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant must retrospectively adjust its financial statements for the most recently completed fiscal year to give effect to the as‑if pooling‑of‑interests. Use those restated financial statements to determine significance of subsequent acquisitions. The investment test is performed differently for transactions involving prior common control combinations (see referenced guidance in handbook chapter 3.4.150). Worked example demonstrates recalculation of asset significance using retrospectively adjusted totals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common‑control combination investment test alternative metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: For combinations between entities or businesses under common control, the investment test is met when either (a) the net book value of the tested subsidiary exceeds 10% of the registrant’s consolidated total assets, or (b) the number of common shares exchanged by the registrant exceeds 10% of its total common shares outstanding at the date the combination is initiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paragraph (B) of S‑X Rule 1‑02(w)(1)(i) provides these alternative 10%‑based tests specifically for common‑control combinations. Use these alternative measures instead of the standard AWMV/total‑assets investment test for such common‑control transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical examples and numeric computation method
rubrics_metrics.description: Worked examples illustrate the step‑by‑step arithmetic for pretax income, revenue and asset components, adjustments for intercompany items, inclusion of advances/loans in consideration, and final significance percentage calculations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: excluding intercompany preferred dividends and investments from income/asset tests; excluding intercompany inventory profit and sales from income and revenue components; excluding intercompany receivables when the acquired business was previously consolidated; including a working capital loan in consideration transferred; including long‑term notes when designated as advances. Use the provided tables and calculations as templates to compute adjusted numerators/denominators and the resulting percentage outcomes to determine significance.
